title: Compiler Module — Snippet Pipeline (Fonts, Text/Math Layout, SVG)
description:
Wave 2 of the compiler-replaces-Typst plan (/Users/ueli/.claude/plans/we-want-to-replace-serialized-pinwheel.md). Follows the syntax-kernel ticket (26/08/04/COMPILER-MODULE-MATH-NOTATION-SYNTAX-KERNEL) which delivered the math_notation parser (MathNode AST) — this ticket makes it renderable.

Deliverable: `compiler::compile_snippet_to_svg(&str, SnippetOptions) -> Result<SvgSnippet, CompileError>` — parses a math notation snippet (compiler_syntax::parse_formula), lays it out using real OpenType MATH-table-driven typesetting, and emits an SVG string, functionally replacing the two Typst call sites (infinite-canvas icon_codec's board_typst_markup_to_svg, animate-core's typst_markup_to_svg) for the next ticket (call-site swap) to consume.

New sub-slots under 🧰️framework/🔨️modules/📚️compiler/: 🌍️world (vendored fonts — Libertinus Math/Serif/Mono, OFL licensed, downloaded from https://github.com/alerque/libertinus releases; reuses the existing checked-in Noto Color Emoji CBDT subset at 🧰️framework/🛍️products/💻️os/🔨️modules/♾️infinite/🖼️canvas/⚡️implementations/🦀️rust/🖼️assets/🔤️NotoColorEmoji-subset.ttf for emoji shortcodes), 🔤️text (shaping via rustybuzz, glyph run model wrapping the external crate behind an interface per CLAUDE.md), 🧮️math (OpenType MATH table layout: sup/sub shift, fraction stack, radical, stretchy delimiter variants, top-accent attachment, horizontal spacing), 🖼️scene (backend-neutral positioned-glyph/rule/image scene model), 📤️svg (own serializer: glyph outlines to path d, emoji to base64 PNG image, usvg-compatible subset).

Known, honestly-scoped v1 simplifications (not gaps to hide): stretchy delimiters use the font's MathVariants glyph-variant list with a vertical-scale fallback when no variant is tall enough (no full non-linear glyph assembly with overlap joining yet); spacing between atoms is fixed-class (thin space around binary/relational operators) not the full MathClass-derived spacing table; emoji shortcode table is a curated common-name set, not exhaustive.
summary:
Delivered Wave 2 of the compiler-replaces-Typst plan: compiler::compile_snippet_to_svg(&str, SnippetOptions) -> Result<SvgSnippet, CompileError> now parses a math notation snippet and renders real, visually-verified SVG — the functional replacement for both existing Typst call sites (call-site swap itself is the next ticket, Wave 3; typst is untouched here).

Four new crates, all cargo check/test/clippy clean:
- semio-framework-compiler-world (🌍️world): vendored fonts — Libertinus Math/Serif/Serif-Italic/Mono (OFL 1.1, downloaded from github.com/alerque/libertinus v7.051) + the existing Noto Color Emoji CBDT subset, ~1.4 MB total vs typst-assets' ~15 MB. License texts included. Only the native EmbeddedFonts provider — the wasm-guest HostAssetFonts provider is real follow-up work for whichever ticket first needs it in a wasm guest.
- semio-framework-compiler-text (🔤️text): wraps rustybuzz/ttf-parser entirely behind owned types (no external type ever appears in its public API) — font loading, HarfBuzz shaping, glyph outline extraction (own SVG-path OutlineBuilder), CBDT/sbix raster extraction, and full OpenType MATH table access (all ~50 MathConstants fields, italics correction, top-accent attachment, stretch variants).
- semio-framework-compiler-math (🧮️math): the actual math layout engine — lays out compiler_syntax's MathNode into a backend-neutral MathBox (positioned glyphs/rules/images), driven by real MATH-table constants: sup/sub shift, fraction stacking, radical with degree, stretchy delimiter variant selection with vertical-scale fallback, top-accent-attached accents, matrix/cases grids, TeX-classic operator spacing, named-symbol table (Greek letters, common operators), upright-function-name detection (sin/cos/lim/...), emoji shortcode → CBDT raster resolution with visible-fallback for unknown shortcodes.
- semio-framework-compiler-svg (📤️svg): own tiny serializer — glyph outlines to `<path>` (per-placement transform bakes translate/scale/Y-flip/stretch), rules to `<rect>`, emoji to base64 `<image>`. No raw text nodes are ever emitted (everything is paths/images), so there's no XML-injection surface to escape against.

Visual verification (not just structural assertions — this is the important part): generated real SVG output for 15 representative snippets (scripts, fractions, radicals, matrices, cases, accents, relations, emoji, greek letters, sin, nested parens) and inspected them rendered in-browser. This caught and fixed THREE real bugs that all 17 unit tests had missed entirely because they only checked structural properties (item counts, presence of a <rect>, etc.), never actual visual correctness:
1. stretched_glyph_box assumed a stretched glyph splits symmetrically (height == depth) around its own origin — false for every glyph tested (a radical sign is almost all ascent; libertinus's '(' has a 4:1 height:depth ratio). Rewrote to center the CHOSEN variant's real bounding box at the target center, deriving height/depth from that bbox instead of assuming symmetry. Fixed both stretchy delimiters and the radical sign.
2. layout_accent centered/placed combining accent glyphs (hat/bar/vec/dot/ddot/tilde) using glyph_hor_advance — which is 0 for combining marks by design, so the accent was placed at the wrong position and effectively invisible. Rewrote to use the glyph's real bounding box for both horizontal centering and vertical placement.
3. root(degree, radicand)'s degree glyph and the radical sign overlapped almost completely — the font's own RadicalKernAfterDegree constant is a large negative value (-0.38em for Libertinus Math) tuned for the font's exact ink-aware notch shape, which a simplified single-box approximation of the degree can't safely replicate; naively trusting it pulled the sign back on top of the degree. Replaced with a small fixed positive gap (documented simplification) — degree now sits cleanly to the left/above, e.g. root(3, x) reads as a legible cube root.

All 48 tests across the six compiler crates (world/text/math/svg/syntax/facade) pass after the fixes; clippy clean (only pre-existing warnings remain, all in dsl_core/dsl_grammar/dsl_notation/dsl_schema — not touched by this ticket). Visual gallery artifacts (gallery.html, zoom.html — before/after screenshots of the bug fixes) left in this ticket's scratch/ folder per the no-delete-scratch-files rule.

Known, honestly-scoped v1 simplifications carried forward from the ticket's original scope (all still true): no full non-linear glyph assembly for stretchy delimiters (variant-or-uniform-scale only), fixed TeX-classic operator spacing rather than a font-derived class table, curated (not exhaustive) emoji shortcode table, single-style-level layout (no display/text-style branching).
